context.text: Blake is currently open to new opportunities and actively exploring roles in forward-deployed engineering, technical product work, or founding-stage teams. He is particularly interested in positions where technical depth and direct impact are not mutually exclusive.

Blake prefers working on genuinely hard problems where he can have direct impact. He values roles that combine architecture, client strategy, and hands-on engineering. He has experience leading cross-functional teams and internal enablement initiatives.

Blake has deep expertise with Cloudflare's edge platform including Workers, D1, Durable Objects, Workflows, KV, R2, and Queues. He builds production applications on this stack and understands the nuances of edge computing patterns, real-time systems, and serverless architecture at scale.

Blake builds agent infrastructure across three layers. The harness: Felix, a managed-agents harness on Cloudflare Workers where manifest-defined agents compile into runtimes exposed over OpenAI-compatible chat, A2A, MCP, and REST/SSE, with swappable session strategies, seven orchestration patterns (ReAct, deep planning, router, parallel fan-out, group-chat, reflect, plan-execute), transport-labelled tool executors, HITL approvals, evals, and an agentic commerce layer (ACP, Stripe, B2B). The memory: Memoturn, a Rust agent-memory database with typed memories, supersession, hybrid recall, and checkpoint/fork/rewind of an agent's mind. The runtime: Fold, a Go platform running containers as Firecracker microVMs with scale-to-zero, built for isolating agent workloads and hosting MCP servers. Earlier iterations ran on AWS Bedrock and AgentCore with LangGraph behind a FastAPI gateway. At Adobe he works with Agent Orchestrator, the agentic layer in Experience Platform. Hands-on with LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, and Claude; he understands prompt engineering, vector search, durable agent memory, human-in-the-loop workflows, and protocol-based agent interop.

Blake has led production implementations for Fortune 500 companies at Adobe. He knows how large systems fail and how to migrate them without breaking things. He has experience with zero-downtime migrations, governance frameworks, and architectural review processes.
